owner: CC owns the code. Akien owns nothing here — the concept is his from common real-world patterns, and the shape is already drawn by the ruling (2026-08-21-feedback-is-probes-two-consumer-kinds).
intention: A TOOL (Law 6: users, not an owner) that records feedback until an LLM inspection pass reads it. The passive consumer's mailbox. A probe targeting a passive consumer (an inspector) writes to the data recorder; the data recorder accumulates records in structured JSON; scheduled-llm-gate-inspection reads the accumulated records and proposes parameter adjustments to the inspector's questions.
why: Akien, 2026-08-21: 'the data recorder was never discussed on how to implement it, but it's so common in the world around me it just seemed a sensible TOOL.' An inspector cannot act on feedback — it has no agency of its own. But it CAN be adjusted: change what questions it asks, change its parameters, change what it measures. That adjustment is the LLM's job (scheduled-llm-gate-inspection). Between the feedback arriving and the LLM reviewing it, the feedback needs somewhere to live. That is the data recorder — a mailbox that holds feedback in structured form, readable by the LLM when the scheduled inspection fires.
traces_to: 2026-08-21-feedback-is-probes-two-consumer-kinds — the ruling that names this tool as the passive consumer's target.
scheduled-llm-gate-inspection — the consumer that reads from this tool.
cairn/tools/feedback — the routing mechanism whose probes write to this tool.
Law 6 — a tool has users, not an owner. This tool's users: probes that write feedback to it, and the scheduled LLM inspection that reads from it.

how.mechanism: THREE operations on a store of structured JSON records: write(record) appends one, read(inspector) returns the accumulated records for a given inspector, clear(ids) removes records after the LLM has processed them. The store is append-only between LLM passes; a pass reads, proposes, and clears the consumed records in one act.
how.record_shape: Each record carries: (1) the feedback finding — what the probe measured; (2) the inspector it targets — whose questions might need adjusting; (3) the probe that fired — so the LLM can trace why this inspector received it; (4) timestamp — when the probe fired; (5) the sieve inputs and outputs at the time — so the LLM sees what the sieve was looking at when the feedback was generated. Structured JSON, not prose — Hex (the M1 Studio box) needs parseable input.
how.storage_location: Under the holder that assembled the inspector, per ruling 2026-08-14-tools-and-machines-remember-under-their-holder: ~/.cairn/devices/<device>/<instance>/tools/data_recorder/<inspector_name>/records.jsonl. JSONL (one record per line) so appending is atomic and reading is streaming. No database — this is a flat-file tool, not relational state.
how.the_tool_class: cairn/tools/data_recorder/ — class definition alongside feedback, diagnostic, etc. Charter (intention+why.json) beside the code. The tool's DEFINITION lives in class-space; its ONGOING state (the accumulated records) lives under the holder in instance-space.
how.read_interface: read(inspector) returns all accumulated records for that inspector as a list. The scheduled-llm-gate-inspection ticket's probe calls read(), feeds the records to Hex, and calls clear() on the ids Hex has consumed. The clear is what prevents unbounded growth — records are ephemeral feedback, not a log.
how.what_this_tool_does_NOT_do: It does not evaluate feedback. It does not propose parameter changes. It does not call an LLM. It does not gate writes. It is a mailbox. The LLM evaluation is scheduled-llm-gate-inspection's job. The parameter change goes through the inspector's own gate (Law 6). This tool holds the records in between.

gates: THREE operations implemented and proved: write(record) appends, read(inspector) returns, clear(ids) removes. Proof teeth: (1) write + read round-trips a structured record; (2) clear removes only the named ids; (3) concurrent writes do not corrupt — JSONL atomic append; (4) read returns empty for an inspector with no accumulated records, not an error; (5) the tool gates no writes at its own address — the Law 6 test (falsifier 1).
falsifier: RED if: (1) the recorder is not a tool — if it gates writes at its own address, it is a machine (Law 6 test); (2) the records are prose rather than structured JSON — Hex needs parseable input; (3) the recorder has its own LLM — the LLM is in the scheduled inspection, not in the recorder; (4) the recorder can ACT on feedback — that makes it an active consumer, and this is the passive case; (5) nobody reads from it — a mailbox nobody opens is a black hole.
watchme: none, because the recorder is a passive tool (Law 6) — its efficacy is measured by the consumer that reads it, not by a probe on the tool itself
horizon: After the feedback tool supports multi-probe charters (a-segments-outbound-edge-carries-one-address). Before scheduled-llm-gate-inspection can fire against real data — that ticket names 'a gate that already collects data in a structured shape' as a dependency, and this tool is that shape.
dependencies: a-segments-outbound-edge-carries-one-address — the multi-probe support that lets a probe target this tool.
scheduled-llm-gate-inspection — the consumer. This tool feeds it.
2026-08-14-tools-and-machines-remember-under-their-holder — the storage location ruling: the recorder's instance data berths under the holder that assembled the inspector.
distinctions_recorded: RECORDER vs CONSUMER: the data recorder HOLDS feedback. The LLM inspection READS and ACTS on it. These are different components.
TOOL vs MACHINE: the data recorder has users (probes write, LLM reads), not an owner. It gates no writes at its own address. If it needed to gate writes, it would be a machine.
PASSIVE CONSUMER'S SHAPE: the inspector is passive — it cannot act on feedback. The data recorder + scheduled LLM inspection together close the loop that an active consumer closes alone.
